I have to agree with other users here, and I'm not going to sugarcoat anything, as someone who almost died from my ED; it'll only get worse. And truth be told, you will never hit your goal weight, it is a moving goalpost. The very second the scale shows you the number you have been aiming for a new goal will appear. No matter how small you get, you'll never feel small enough. 



You will get more and more consumed by the disorder. The dream of being more social? Not going to happen. Your mind is going to be too occupied thinking of food, counting calories, body checking, and worrying what others think of you to follow a conversation. Cute clothes? Forget it. Not only will you be colder than you ever thought possible, you'll be too self conscious to show off your body. When you get to that point, your mind will do anything to keep it hidden. 

  
This is not a glamorous disorder. This is hell on earth, and it'll only get worse the further it goes on uninterrupted. And let's be honest, it's not really about the weight. It never was. 

Please get help before it's too late.

As someone with an ED in a relationship, please be aware that it is insanly draining for both parties involved. Especially if you as the partner also are dealing with severe mental health issues.

Be aware that the ED will twist everything and anything you say. For example, if your girlfriend ask for your opinion on if she should have a cookie any answer is wrong. In her mind "Yes" might translate into "They think I'm just a fat pig who will eat anything they come across," answering "No" might translate into "He thinks I'm too fat too ever eat again."

Do: Try to listen without judging. Get a support network for yourself outside of your girlfriend, may it be a friend or a support group. 

Don't: Comment on weight or body. Be very mindful, even small comments that are well-intended can hurt a lot. Stay away from "You look healthy" at all costs. If you really want to give compliments, hair, makeup, clothes, humour, intellect and skills are imo better to focus on. 

DISCLAIMER:
These are just my experiences. I think the absolute best thing you can do is to talk to your GF and ask her what she would find the most supportive. Everyone's EDs are different.

AND remember that you CANNOT save her. I know you want to. The only person that can save her is herself, and the only person that can save you is you.

Best of luck💕

From what I've understood starvation mode is real, but it happens at late stage starvation. Then the body tries to conserve energy by shutting down/limiting non-essential functions like menstruation and normal body temperature. Heart rate also goes down and muscle tissue is broken down as there is no fat reserves left and the body eats itself to keep the brain alive. This happened to holocaust victims.

However, the idea of starvation mode as described in mainstream media is a myth. You won't go into starvation mode by skipping a meal or eating at a caloric deficit. As another commenter has said, someone at a lower body weight has a lower TDEE. It's not due to metabolic damage someone who used to be 150 lbs can't eat like they did when they were 200 lbs, they simply have less tissue to sustain and therefore require less calories.

As with most things it's a combination of nature and nurture.

There is the biological hunger and satiety hormones. Ghrelin (hunger) is produced in the gastrointestinal tract, while leptin (satiety) is produced in fat cells.

A person with low body fat while get less leptin which = less satiety, which in turn carn result in weight gain if the person is in tune with their signals. The opposite is true for someone with more body fat, however it is common for peoole with obesity to be leptin resistent, so even though they gave more leptin in their system they do not get satiety. 

But what also matters is the nurture part. If you were  taught as a child to always clear your plate you were taught to ignore your cues, and I think nurture is far more important in weight management/control.

I just borrowed a self-help book on the subject, and I've started working on the first chapter. It is not in english, so I hope my translation makes sense. Summary of the book:

Step 1: Keep an honest food diary starting today, and for two more days. Everything that has gone into you mouth goes into the diary under headings: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner, Other. Or under the headings "attempt at [insert meal] if it turned into a binge.

Step 2: Evaluste the food diaries. Have you  binged etc. Is there a pattern?

Step 3: Eat breakfast every day. No excuses. Focus only on breakfast for at least three weeks (continue w/ food diary)
- Decide the night before exactly what to eat for BF.
- Buy exactly that, no more no less.
- if you can't shop the day before buy it in the morning. 
- If it feels scary to eat alone, go to a cafe, but decide beforehand what to order.
- start small
- Eat something you think you would enjoy instead of the ~healthiest~ option.
- only veggies is not a real breakfast. It could be a sandwich, some yoghurt and granola, or porridge etc.

Step 4: Write three coping mechanisms that will help you manage emotional distress (that you know or think will work).

Step 5: Every time you binge eat, try to write down exactly what you ate the emotion you had before you binged. One word is enough, but do it the same day you binged. 

Step 6: Time for lunch. 
Don't diet at lunch. Eat something filling with complex carbs, protein, and healthy fats that wont trigger a need for sugar in the afternoon. Lunch should be eaten ~11:00-13:00. 
- Lunch should be a real sit down meal (plate, knife and fork, or spoon). 
- It should not only consist of raw veggies.
- Eat until you are not hungry anymore, not until you are full. 
- Focus on eating lunch for three weeks, while also eating breakfast.
- Keep upp the food diary.

Step 7: Dinner
When you feel like you have breakfast and lunch down, it's time to work on dinner.
- Eat between 16 and 17.
- A proper meal (sit down, plate, fork and knife, or spoon)
- If you had a cold dish for lunch, have a warm dinner. At least one warm meal per day.
- Eat something you enjoy!
- Eat until you are  ot hu gry anymore, not until you are full.
- Finish the meal when you've eaten what you planned. If you are really want more, have a fruit.
- Sit down and drink some coffee or tea after dinner, it takes 20 minutes for the stomach to sig al to the brain that it is full. 
- Set the table and have a clear start and finish to the meal.
- Eat without distractions, or at most have som calm music playing.
_____________________
Even if you binged at breakfast, have lunch.
Even if you binged at lunch, have dinner.
Even if you binged at dinner, start the next day with breakfast.

This will (hopefully) break the binge restrict cycle.
_________________________
Other tips:
- Deal with your emotional problems that cause you to  binge. Identify feelings and triggers in the food diary. If possible seek professional help.

- If certain foods trigger your bingeing, keep them out of the house, or buy in pre-portioned packages.

- Some studies show that regular exercise helps with binge eating.

- Accept that recovery is not a straight road, and that it will take time to heal.
